decisions.question: The pinned Flutter SDK on this machine has no engine artifacts (bin/cache/pkg/sky_engine and bin/cache/artifacts are absent), so no real `flutter test --no-pub` can run and no workspace with flutter_test resolves; fetching them is a network action outside the run rules. How does the plan verify the Flutter runner that the phase's Verification names?

options.label: stand-in Flutter SDK, real flutter Outstanding
options.consequence: The tool's tests run a testWidgets binding through a stand-in SDK laid out as {sdk}/bin/flutter and {sdk}/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart (scripts over the real dart) and a stand-in flutter_test package, pinning the runner choice, the flutter path, the exact command line, the filter and the report parsing; the real flutter's behavior rests on its flutter_tools 3.47.7 source and stays Outstanding, deferred to nidana.flutter.2, the first gate that starts it through the tool.

options.label: fetch the Flutter artifacts
options.consequence: A real flutter test run in the tool's tests, at the cost of a network action beyond pub.dev that the run rules forbid without the owner.

options.label: stop the step
options.consequence: No plan until the owner provides the artifacts; the tool lane stalls although everything but the last confirmation can be built and tested now.

decisions.chosen: stand-in Flutter SDK, real flutter Outstanding
decisions.why: The tool's side of the Flutter runner (which bindings, which executable, which arguments, how the report is read) is fully testable with a stand-in, and flutter_tools 3.47.7 hands `-r json` and `--name` to package:test unchanged and returns its exit code, so the JSON the stand-in produces is the protocol the real runner prints. What a stand-in cannot show (the real tool from a pure-Dart root on a binding under hsdd/) has earlier evidence from contract-fixtures Q10 and Q11 on another machine. nidana.flutter.1 needs the artifacts anyway to create its member. The owner would have been asked whether to fetch them.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-step-preamble.md Run rules, Dangerous or outside actions

decisions.question: ADR-001 item 4 says a conformance library imports neither package:test nor package:flutter_test, and no set checks it (routed from S101). Which set checks it?

options.label: structure rule conformance-import
options.consequence: Checked at every gate, needs no implementation, reported at the conformance library's path; structure gains a rule item 9's list does not name, which item 12 (structure checks item 3 and the items for the contract's kind) covers.

options.label: behavior set, per binding
options.consequence: Checked only where a binding runs and only for bound libraries, so a default gate never sees it; a binding fails for its suite's defect.

options.label: leave it unchecked
options.consequence: A suite that imports flutter_test would make a binding chosen for dart test fail to load, a defect found late and read as the implementation's.

decisions.chosen: structure rule conformance-import
decisions.why: The rule is a property of the fixture text, like the case-name rule structure already checks in conformance libraries, and ADR-001 item 12 makes structure the checker of item 3 and the items for the kind once the tool exists. The runner choice depends on it: the tool picks the runner from the binding's own imports, which is only sound while suites import neither test package. No committed conformance library violates it.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases (S101 Task 5)

decisions.question: When a binding names an absent package and the --guarantee restriction also admits none of its cases, is it PENDING or a pass with no case run?

options.label: PENDING first
options.consequence: A restricted replay before the producing package exists reports the binding PENDING and exits 1, as ADR-001's Consequences say of every fixture that names the package.

options.label: restriction first
options.consequence: The binding passes unrun, so a too-early restricted gate can pass its behavior set while the package is absent.

decisions.chosen: PENDING first
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 lists a binding among the fixtures that are PENDING when they import an absent package, and its Consequences say a replay whose producing package is absent reports every fixture that names it as PENDING so that a gate placed too early fails. The not-admitted rule exists so that no runner starts with an empty filter; a PENDING binding starts none either, so both rules hold. The order within a binding: unreadable binding or unresolvable suite (FAIL), absent package (PENDING), restriction admits none (PASS, not run), run.

decisions.question: Which imports decide that a binding is PENDING: the binding's own, or also those of the conformance library it imports?

options.label: binding and its suite
options.consequence: A binding whose suite imports an absent package is PENDING, never a load failure that reads as a defect.

options.label: the binding alone
options.consequence: Simpler, and enough for every committed binding today (each imports its implementing package directly), but a suite that imports a package its binding does not would fail to load.

decisions.chosen: binding and its suite
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 makes PENDING any behavior library that imports an absent package, and a conformance library is a behavior library; the binding cannot load without it. The scope's 'which is why bindings import the implementing package directly' still holds: the direct import is what lets the tool see the implementing package. Other relative imports of a binding (none are committed) are not read.

decisions.question: One runner process per binding, or one per group of bindings that share a runner and a filter?

options.label: one process per binding
options.consequence: Counts and failing names belong to one binding without reading suite paths from the report, each binding gets the filter of its own suite's slug, and a load failure stays with its binding; about 0.5 to 1 s of runner start per binding.

options.label: batch by runner and filter
options.consequence: Fewer runner starts, but outcomes must be attributed by the paths the runner prints (relative under dart test, absolute file URIs under flutter test), which differ between the runners and under linked roots.

decisions.chosen: one process per binding
decisions.why: Ten committed bindings at 0.5 to 1 s each is cheap next to what they test, and attribution by process is exact; dart test prints the path as given while flutter test hands package:test absolute file URIs, so path-based attribution would differ per runner. Bindings run one after another, so concurrent flutter runs never contend for its startup lock.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/behavior-set-plan/output.txt D1 to D10, R1 to R3 (seconds)

decisions.question: What does the one line per binding say, given that FixtureOutcome is Passed, Failed or Pending and a Passed line carries no detail?

options.label: Passed gains a detail; failures are problems
options.consequence: PASS lines read 'PASS behavior {path}: {p} passed, 0 failed, {s} skipped under {runner}' (with ', restricted to {slug} {ids}' under --guarantee) or 'not run: ...'; FAIL lines list a cases problem with the counts, then one failed-case problem per failing name; load failures a load problem. No new outcome type, every existing line unchanged.

options.label: a fourth outcome type for runs
options.consequence: Typed counts in the outcome, but every exhaustive switch over FixtureOutcome (report, tally, exit code) changes, and nidana.model.7 inherits it.

decisions.chosen: Passed gains a detail; failures are problems
decisions.why: The scope asks for counts and failing names on one line; an optional detail on Passed and the existing problem list carry both while every set keeps one outcome model. The counts always print all three numbers, as the summary line does, so the line has one form.

decisions.question: How does the tool tell a binding that did not load from one whose cases failed, in package:test's JSON report?

options.label: a visible failed test with no group
options.consequence: Every real test sits in the suite's root group (groupIDs non-empty), while the load pseudo-test has groupIDs [] and is hidden when the load succeeds; the rule needs no test name.

options.label: a test named 'loading {path}'
options.consequence: Depends on the path form the runner prints, which differs between dart test and flutter test.

options.label: the runner's exit code
options.consequence: dart test exits 1 for both a load failure and a failing case, so it cannot tell them apart.

decisions.chosen: a visible failed test with no group
decisions.why: The experiment shows the shape directly: a load failure is a non-hidden test with groupIDs [] and result error (D6, D7, D9), a loaded suite's load test is hidden (D1), and top-level cases carry the root group's id (D1). The detail shown is the first non-blank text after 'Failed to load "{path}":'.

decisions.question: A runner that ran no case (a filter the reader admitted but no runtime name matches, or a binding that registers nothing; dart test exits 79 with done success true): pass or fail?

options.label: FAIL: no case ran
options.consequence: A binding that registers its cases under other names, or none, fails loudly; the not-admitted pass stays reserved for what the reader shows the restriction excludes.

options.label: PASS like a not-admitted binding
options.consequence: A binding that runs nothing passes every gate.

decisions.chosen: FAIL: no case ran
decisions.why: The tool starts a runner only when the reader shows an admitted case, so zero cases at run time means the binding does not register what its suite lists: a defect. The JSON's done success is true in that case (D4, D8), so the tool decides from the visible-test count, never from success alone.

decisions.question: No flutter in the SDK of the running dart, or a runner that prints no complete JSON report: how are these reported?

options.label: SetUnavailable for the slug's behavior set
options.consequence: ERROR behavior {slug}: {reason} on stderr and exit 2, as ADR-001 item 9 names for a missing flutter; the no-flutter case is decided before any binding of the slug starts.

options.label: FAIL the one binding
options.consequence: Other bindings' outcomes survive, but an environment error reads as a fixture defect and the exit is 1, not 2.

decisions.chosen: SetUnavailable for the slug's behavior set
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 and nidana.model D2 item 1 name no flutter beside the running dart for a Flutter binding as an environment error, exit 2; a runner with no report is the same class as a dart analyze with no JSON report, which nidana.model.2 made SetUnavailable. Deciding the flutter check before running spares the slug's dart bindings a run whose results would be discarded.

decisions.question: How is 'the flutter that belongs to the SDK of the dart running the tool' found?

options.label: strict layout {root}/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart
options.consequence: The dart belongs to a Flutter SDK only when it sits there; the flutter is {root}/bin/flutter (flutter.bat beside dart.exe) and must exist; any other dart has no flutter.

options.label: four directories up, no name check
options.consequence: Finds the same file on a Flutter SDK, but names an unrelated path for a standalone Dart SDK.

options.label: flutter on PATH
options.consequence: Could run another SDK's flutter than the dart running the tool, which item 9 rules out.

decisions.chosen: strict layout {root}/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart
decisions.why: Platform.resolvedExecutable under fvm is ~/fvm/versions/3.47.7/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart and the flutter at ~/fvm/versions/3.47.7/bin/flutter exists (T1); the name check makes the rule say what item 9 says, and the stand-in SDK of the tests reproduces the layout.

decisions.question: A Dart fixture that is not UTF-8 makes readSnapshot throw and the replay exit 2 (routed from S103). How does it become a fixture failure?

options.label: undecodable map on the snapshot; structure reports it
options.consequence: readSnapshot decodes source bytes itself; a file that is not UTF-8 keeps a null source and its reason in SlugSnapshot.undecodable; structure fails it with an encoding problem (exit 1); surface, reject and behavior skip a library they cannot read, and the behavior set fails a binding or suite it cannot read.

options.label: a sealed source type in files
options.consequence: Every reader of SlugSnapshot.files changes for one edge case.

decisions.chosen: undecodable map on the snapshot; structure reports it
decisions.why: Structure runs first at every replay, so the failure is always reported and the exit is 1; an optional field with a const empty default leaves every existing construction of SlugSnapshot unchanged. The reason reads 'not UTF-8: {message} (at offset {n})', the schema set's wording for documents.

decisions.question: Validating --guarantee ids against the slug's declared guarantees (routed from S101): what does an undeclared id give, and when is it checked?

options.label: usage error 64, before any snapshot
options.consequence: 'unknown guarantee {slug}/G{n}: hsdd/contract/{slug}.md declares no G{n}' and the usage text, exit 64; the shell reads only the contract texts of the slugs the restriction names, so the check runs before anything else is read or started.

options.label: a structure failure
options.consequence: The replay runs and fails at exit 1, so a typo reads as a fixture defect.

options.label: no validation
options.consequence: A typo admits no case and the restricted binding passes unrun, which ADR-001 item 9 permits.

decisions.chosen: usage error 64, before any snapshot
decisions.why: An id that names no guarantee is a command line that names no Request, the same class as an unknown slug, which is also checked against the files; item 9's list of usage errors begins 'such as'. Ids are never renumbered, so a gate's id is always declared.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases (S101 final review)

decisions.question: Moving findWorkspaceRoot out of shell.dart so conformance libraries stop compiling the tool (routed from S104): where, and what then holds dart:io?

options.label: lib/src/workspace.dart, pinned by a test
options.consequence: fixture.dart imports json_document.dart and workspace.dart only; dart:io is allowed in shell.dart and workspace.dart alone, and a package test reads the directives to pin both.

options.label: leave it in shell.dart
options.consequence: Every binding compiles the whole tool through fixture.dart.

decisions.chosen: lib/src/workspace.dart, pinned by a test
decisions.why: Every behavior run now compiles fixture.dart's imports; the shell drags in args, package_config and every set. The move is one function and its helpers, and a directive test keeps the rule from drifting.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases (S104 final review)

decisions.question: A progress line for long test runs (routed from S104): where and when?

options.label: stderr, one line per binding started
options.consequence: 'running behavior {path} under {runner}' before each runner starts; stdout keeps one line per fixture and the summary; no line for PENDING, failed-before-run or not-admitted bindings.

options.label: print each set's lines as it completes
options.consequence: Progress at set granularity only; a slug's behavior set still runs silently.

options.label: none
options.consequence: An unrestricted --all with Flutter bindings runs silently for minutes.

decisions.chosen: stderr, one line per binding started
decisions.why: Runs are still computed before printing, as the analysis requires, so a progress signal has to be separate from the report; stderr keeps stdout's line-per-fixture form, and the exit code stays the gate's signal.

decisions.question: A conformance library that no binding in any slug imports should cover nothing (routed from S101, needs a cross-slug view). Does this plan take it?

options.label: leave it routed, to the end-of-node sweep
options.consequence: Coverage keeps counting every case name as ADR-001 item 3 reads today; nothing changes for any committed contract, since every committed conformance library is imported by a binding (R7).

options.label: take it in this phase
options.consequence: structure would read every slug's bindings on every replay instead of one snapshot and change what item 3's coverage counts, a seventh concern in a six-task sitting.

decisions.chosen: leave it routed, to the end-of-node sweep
decisions.why: It changes the structure set's coverage rule, which ADR-001 item 3 defines (a case covers the id its name begins with; it says nothing of being bound), so it is a reading for hsdd-adr before it is code, and it gives structure a workspace-wide input. It is outside the behavior set, the cap is reached, and today it changes no verdict. The signal that would bring it forward: a contract authored with a suite no binding imports.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases (S101 final review)

decisions.question: The phase Verification says 'once nidana.model.5 has merged, topic-model@v1's binding loads and its cases fail on UnimplementedError, not on loading'. Against the merged declarations the binding loads, 9 of 41 cases pass, and of the 32 failures 27 are UnimplementedError and 5 are expectation failures (identity equality, an uncopied list). What does this phase check, and how?

options.label: check load against case failure; record the kinds
options.consequence: The tool's tests pin that a binding that does not compile reports load and one whose bodies throw reports cases with failed-case names; the verification doc records the real replay of topic-model --set behavior (a cases line, no load problem) and the experiment's breakdown of the 32 by first error, and reads 'fail on UnimplementedError' as failing on what nidana.model D3 leaves undelivered: bodies that throw UnimplementedError, and Object's == and toString.

options.label: make the tool classify failures
options.consequence: The line would say how many failures are UnimplementedError, a reading of error texts the ADR does not ask for, to satisfy one sentence.

options.label: hold the sentence literally
options.consequence: The phase would fail its own Verification on facts D3 decided (equality stays Object's until nidana.model.8).

decisions.chosen: check load against case failure; record the kinds
decisions.why: The sentence's point is 'not on loading': the binding compiles against the real declarations. The tool's line separates a load failure from case failures, which is what a gate needs; which exception a case dies of is the implementation's state, and D3 says plainly that equality and toString stay Object's in the type-level phases, so those five failures are the same undelivered state. The gate does not run --set behavior over the committed tree, so the verification doc shows it by a recorded manual replay and the experiment's breakdown.

decisions.question: How are the phase's deliverables and the routed items split into at most 6 tasks?

options.label: plumbing, structure, plans, reports, shell, verification
options.consequence: Task 1 the routed replay plumbing and restriction fixes; Task 2 the two structure rules; Task 3 the pure binding plans; Task 4 the pure report reading and outcomes; Task 5 the shell with the runner tests; Task 6 the gate and the doc. Each pure task reviews on its own; the cap is reached.

options.label: fold the routed items into the shell task
options.consequence: Room for the cross-slug coverage item, but one task mixing usage errors, encoding and process running that a reviewer cannot reject separately.

decisions.chosen: plumbing, structure, plans, reports, shell, verification
decisions.why: Pure before shell, as the node's ordering policy says inside the tool; the plumbing goes first so the behavior set is written once against the context record and the reordered parse. The phase estimate (about 300 lines) is far below what nidana.model.1 and .2 measured (about 9 times their estimates), so the split favors reviewable tasks over fewer ones.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md Phase Plan (the replay tool bullet)

decisions.question: A binding of one slug imports another slug's conformance library (bus-api's bus_activation_test.dart and topology-dsl's live suite), which the replayed slug's snapshot does not hold. How does the pure planner see it?

options.label: the shell reads that slug's snapshot
options.consequence: suiteSlugs(snapshot) names the slugs a binding's relative imports reach; the shell reads each such slug that has a fixture directory with readSnapshot, so the same reader, hidden-entry rule and UTF-8 handling apply; planBindings looks the suite up in the map.

options.label: the shell reads the one file
options.consequence: Fewer bytes read, but a second reading path for Dart sources with its own absent and not-UTF-8 handling.

decisions.chosen: the shell reads that slug's snapshot
decisions.why: One reading path for every Dart source keeps the pure core's input one type; a snapshot costs milliseconds. A suite slug with no fixture directory is not read, and the binding fails with 'does not exist'.

decisions.question: Seeded workspaces for the runner tests need package:test, package:matcher, package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart and package:flutter_test to resolve offline; the real tool package cannot join a temporary workspace and the real flutter_test cannot resolve here. What do the tests seed?

options.label: stand-in members nidana_contract_check and flutter_test
options.consequence: The seeded conformance library imports package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart as committed ones do (a stand-in holding the ConformanceCase typedef), and the widget binding imports package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart (a stand-in exporting package:test with testWidgets over test), so runner choice, PENDING and the runs see the committed import forms.

options.label: local typedefs and no flutter_test
options.consequence: Simpler seeds, but the Flutter binding could not be chosen by its import, and the suite would not import fixture.dart as ADR-001 item 4 requires.

decisions.chosen: stand-in members nidana_contract_check and flutter_test
decisions.why: W1 shows the four-member workspace resolves offline in 0.2 s with test 1.33.0 and matcher 0.12.20 from the pub cache, and D10 and F1 show the stand-in testWidgets binding runs under dart test and under the stand-in flutter.

decisions.question: Under --guarantee, which ids form a binding's filter, and what does its line say?

options.label: every id of the suite's slug, ascending, named on the line
options.consequence: The filter is '^(G2|G5) ' from the restriction's ids of the slug whose suite the binding imports; the line ends ', restricted to {slug} {ids}', so a reader sees which suite's ids ran.

options.label: only the ids some case begins with
options.consequence: A shorter filter, but the line no longer shows the restriction as given.

decisions.chosen: every id of the suite's slug, ascending, named on the line
decisions.why: Both admit the same cases (an id no case begins with matches nothing); the restriction as given is what a gate author wrote. The filter is built from ids alone, never from case text, so no case name needs escaping, and the trailing space anchors G2 against G25 (D2).
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md nidana.model.6 Scope (for G2 and G5, ^(G2|G5) )

decisions.question: Which files does the behavior set run as bindings?

options.label: every behavior/{name}_test.dart directly under behavior/
options.consequence: The structure set's binding pattern; a present but unlisted binding still runs and structure reports it unlisted; conformance libraries and nested files get no behavior line.

options.label: only the bindings ## Validation lists
options.consequence: An unlisted binding, which structure already fails, would also go unrun, hiding what it does.

decisions.chosen: every behavior/{name}_test.dart directly under behavior/
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 4 names bindings by their file form, and structure already holds the listing rule; running what is present keeps the two sets independent.

experiments.question: What does `dart test --reporter json` print and exit with from a workspace root over bindings under hsdd/contract/fixture/ (every case, anchored filters, a filter that admits none, another slug's suite, a binding that does not compile, an absent package, no case, a main that throws); where is the flutter of the running dart's SDK and can it run here; what does flutter_tools 3.47.7 accept and hand to package:test; can a temporary workspace with stand-in nidana_contract_check and flutter_test members resolve offline and run a testWidgets binding through a stand-in SDK; do the committed bindings nidana.model implements load, and what do their cases fail on; do the plan's own seeded samples behave and pass structure as the plan expects?
experiments.finding: The JSON reporter prints only JSON events (protocol 0.1.1); a loaded suite's load pseudo-test is hidden, a load failure is a visible error test with groupIDs [] whose error begins 'Failed to load "{path}":' (D0b, D6, D7, D9); real cases have a non-empty groupIDs (D0, D1); a filter admitting nothing or a binding with no case ends with done success true and exit 79 (D4, D8); '^(G2) ' admits G2 and not G25 (D2, D3). Platform.resolvedExecutable is ~/fvm/versions/3.47.7/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart and ~/fvm/versions/3.47.7/bin/flutter exists (T1), but the SDK has no engine artifacts (bin/cache/pkg/sky_engine and bin/cache/artifacts absent, T2), so no real flutter test can run here; flutter_tools 3.47.7 allows --reporter json, a repeatable --name with splitCommas false, requires pubspec.yaml in the working directory and test_api in the package configuration, passes -r json and --name to package:test, hands test files as absolute URIs and returns package:test's exit code (T3). The stand-in workspace resolves offline in 0.2 s (W1) and the stand-in SDK runs a testWidgets binding with the recorded call 'test --no-pub --reporter json --name ^(G2|G5)  {path}' (F1). topic-model@v1's binding loads: 41 cases, 9 pass, 32 fail (27 UnimplementedError, 5 expectation failures on identity equality and an uncopied list); topology-dsl's recording binding 0 of 24 pass, topology-ir's 1 of 43, all loading (R1 to R3); the tool's fixture reader reads exactly those case counts (R6); no committed conformance library imports a test package (R5), every one is imported by a binding and only the two flutter-binding bindings import flutter_test (R7). The plan's samples give 2 passed, 2 failed under dart test, 2 passed for '^(G2) ', 2 passed and 1 failed for the host binding under '^(G2|G3) ', a load failure 'Undefined name' for the broken binding (P1), and pass structure with 7 and 3 fixtures (P2). utf8.decode reports 'Invalid UTF-8 byte' at offset 3 for the seeded bytes (U1).
